findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:145 — [P1, confidence 100] `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` — Storing all single-use codes in one encrypted user field forces an unguarded read-modify-write, so two concurrent logins with the same backup code both authenticate before either whole-field update invalidates it.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 — [P2, confidence 75] `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));` — The exact case-sensitive lookup rejects an uppercase transcription of the displayed hexadecimal backup code because the setup path stores lowercase hex and the verification path normalizes dashes but not case.

packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — [P1, confidence 100] `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN     "backupCodes" TEXT;` — Existing 2FA users receive no backup codes, and the change adds no settings action or API to generate replacements, so migrated users and users who exhaust their codes cannot use the backup-code recovery feature despite the UI directing them to generate codes in settings.

packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — [P1, confidence 100] `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN     "backupCodes" TEXT;` — Adding the schema change to the pre-existing, previously empty `20230804153419_add_backup_codes` migration leaves every database that already recorded that migration without the `backupCodes` column, so the newly deployed reads and writes fail at runtime instead of migrating those installations.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — [P2, confidence 100] `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"));` — Clipboard permission denial rejects without a handler while line 279 immediately reports success, so the user is told the backup codes were copied when nothing reached the clipboard.

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 — [P2, confidence 75] `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` — A malformed or no-longer-decryptable stored backup-code payload throws outside error handling and returns the framework's raw 500 response instead of the endpoint's JSON error shape, leaving the disable flow unable to present an honest actionable result.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:71 — [P3, confidence 75] `const resetState = () => { setPassword(""); setErrorMessage(null); setStep(SetupStep.ConfirmPassword); };` — Closing or cancelling after entering a TOTP leaves `form.totpCode`, the secret, backup codes, and the object URL alive, so a later setup attempt reuses stale wizard state and retains every generated download blob until another successful setup replaces it.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — [P2, confidence 100] `tabIndex={-1}` — This unrelated global PasswordField change removes every password-visibility control from sequential keyboard navigation, so a 2FA backup-code feature silently degrades keyboard access on login and settings forms across the application.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:121 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode) {` — Supplying any nonempty `totpCode` alongside a valid backup code skips password verification, so possession of one backup code alone authenticates as the victim and defeats the intended two-factor boundary.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 — [P1, confidence 100] `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` — The assertion checks that the Promise returned by `isChecked()` is truthy instead of awaiting its boolean result, so the enable-2FA test passes when the switch remains unchecked and the feature failed to enable.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — [P1, confidence 100] `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` — The only modified 2FA test never submits a backup code through login or disable, so regressions in both newly added recovery paths ship green despite those paths being the feature's core behavior.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — [P2, confidence 100] `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt");` — The download test verifies only the filename, so an empty or incorrectly formatted backup-code file passes even though users cannot recover their accounts from the downloaded artifact.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:121 — [P2, confidence 100] `await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor();` — The copy test verifies only a success toast and never reads the clipboard, so a rejected or empty clipboard write passes while users are falsely told their recovery codes were copied.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — [P1, confidence 100] `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN     "backupCodes" TEXT;` — Existing 2FA users receive no backup codes, and the change adds no settings action or API to generate replacements, so migrated users and users who exhaust their codes cannot use the backup-code recovery feature despite the UI directing them to generate codes in settings.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration adds a nullable backupCodes column, but existing users with 2FA enabled will have NULL backupCodes. The diff shows the UI displays 'missing_backup_codes' error message directing users to 'generate them in your settings', but there's no API endpoint or settings UI added to generate new backup codes for existing users. The setup.ts only generates codes during initial 2FA setup. This means existing 2FA users cannot use backup code recovery, and users who exhaust their codes have no way to regenerate them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — [P1, confidence 100] `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN     "backupCodes" TEXT;` — Adding the schema change to the pre-existing, previously empty `20230804153419_add_backup_codes` migration leaves every database that already recorded that migration without the `backupCodes` column, so the newly deployed reads and writes fail at runtime instead of migrating those installations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is a 'pre-existing, previously empty' migration file, but the diff clearly shows this is a NEW file being added (indicated by 'new file mode 100644' and the +++ /dev/null to +++ path pattern). This is not modifying an existing empty migration - it's creating a new migration file with the proper ALTER TABLE statement. The migration system will correctly apply this to databases that haven't run it yet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — [P2, confidence 100] `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"));` — Clipboard permission denial rejects without a handler while line 279 immediately reports success, so the user is told the backup codes were copied when nothing reached the clipboard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows on line 278-279 that navigator.clipboard.writeText() is called and immediately followed by showToast(t('backup_codes_copied'), 'success') on the next line. The clipboard API returns a Promise that can reject if permission is denied, but there's no .then()/.catch() or try/catch handling. If the clipboard write fails, the success toast will still be shown, misleading the user into thinking the codes were copied when they weren't.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that at line 58 in disable.ts, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is called outside of any try-catch block. If the stored backupCodes are malformed or decryption fails, this will throw an unhandled exception, resulting in a raw 500 error instead of the structured JSON error response the endpoint normally returns. The existing try-catch in the handler only wraps the password verification section, not this backup code decryption logic. This is a real defect in error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — [P2, confidence 100] `tabIndex={-1}` — This unrelated global PasswordField change removes every password-visibility control from sequential keyboard navigation, so a 2FA backup-code feature silently degrades keyboard access on login and settings forms across the application.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows tabIndex={-1} being added to the password visibility toggle button in the PasswordField component. This is a shared UI component used across the application. Setting tabIndex={-1} removes the button from keyboard tab navigation, which is an accessibility regression. While the finding correctly identifies this as degrading keyboard access, the change appears intentional (likely to prevent the toggle from interrupting form field navigation). However, this does affect accessibility for users who rely on keyboard navigation to toggle password visibility. The finding is accurate about the behavioral change, though whether it's a 'bug' vs intentional UX decision is debatable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:121 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode) {` — Supplying any nonempty `totpCode` alongside a valid backup code skips password verification, so possession of one backup code alone authenticates as the victim and defeats the intended two-factor boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code flow. Looking at the diff in next-auth-options.ts, the password verification happens BEFORE the 2FA check (lines 119-126 check password first). The condition at line 121 `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` is checking whether to throw an error for missing totpCode when password exists - it's not skipping password verification. The actual flow is: 1) verify password (lines 119-126), 2) then check 2FA via backup code OR totp code (lines 128-165). The backup code path at line 128 `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` only runs AFTER password has been verified. Supplying a totpCode alongside a backup code doesn't skip password verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 — [P1, confidence 100] `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` — The assertion checks that the Promise returned by `isChecked()` is truthy instead of awaiting its boolean result, so the enable-2FA test passes when the switch remains unchecked and the feature failed to enable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the test code. Looking at line 48-49 in the diff, the code `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` is indeed problematic. The `isChecked()` method returns a Promise<boolean>, and without awaiting it before passing to `toBeTruthy()`, the assertion checks if the Promise object is truthy (which it always is), not the actual boolean result. The diff even includes a FIXME comment at lines 47-48 acknowledging this issue: 'FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked, compare to test below which checks for data-state="checked" and works as expected'. This is a real test bug that could mask failures in the 2FA enable functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — [P1, confidence 100] `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` — The only modified 2FA test never submits a backup code through login or disable, so regressions in both newly added recovery paths ship green despite those paths being the feature's core behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file adds a TODO comment about missing backup code tests, and the actual test code only tests the backup codes display/download/copy functionality after enabling 2FA, but never tests logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with a backup code. The diff shows new backup code login logic in next-auth-options.ts and backup code disable logic in disable.ts, but the test file doesn't exercise these paths. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — [P2, confidence 100] `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt");` — The download test verifies only the filename, so an empty or incorrectly formatted backup-code file passes even though users cannot recover their accounts from the downloaded artifact.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 116 only verifies the filename of the downloaded backup codes file, not its content. The diff shows a TODO comment at line 118 acknowledging this: '// TODO: check file content'. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added backup code functionality - if the file generation is broken, the test would still pass. However, this is not a bug (the feature code itself appears correct), but rather an incomplete test for new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:121 — [P2, confidence 100] `await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor();` — The copy test verifies only a success toast and never reads the clipboard, so a rejected or empty clipboard write passes while users are falsely told their recovery codes were copied.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 121 only verifies a toast appears but doesn't actually verify the clipboard content. Looking at the diff, the test does `await page.getByTestId('backup-codes-copy').click()` followed by `await page.getByTestId('toast-success').waitFor()` with a TODO comment acknowledging 'check clipboard content'. This is a legitimate test coverage gap - the test doesn't verify the actual clipboard write succeeded with correct content. However, this is not a bug in the application code itself, but rather incomplete test coverage for the new backup codes feature. The application code in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx does call `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`, so the functionality exists - it's just not fully tested.
